subject: barnstormerBiplane
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: barnstormer biplane.
Style: whimsical.
reasoning:
I'm deciding to keep this as a static model without joints, maybe just a decorative propeller element, and sketching out a whimsical 1920s biplane design facing forward with a chubby, playful fuselage shape.

Mapping out the biplane's components now - fuselage, cowling, wings, tail, wheels, pilot - with pastel colors and exaggerated proportions, working through the geometry for the lofted fuselage body and lathed cowling shape around the nose.

Writing wing extrusion code...

I'm adjusting the lower wing position to attach beneath the fuselage, then planning the strut geometry—interplane struts connecting lower and upper wings, cabane struts linking the fuselage top to the upper wing, plus thin rigging wires between them. Now I'm starting to lay out the tail fin's side-view outline.

Adjusting the stabilizer taper, then adding cylindrical wheels with dark tires and cream hubs, V-shaped landing gear struts connecting the fuselage underside to the wheels, a small tail skid wheel, and now starting on the nose spinner and propeller blade geometry.

For the cockpit I'm adding a dark raised box with a rim frame on top of the fuselage, then building the pilot with a skin-toned head and torso, leather cap, goggles made from cylinders and a strap, and a flowing scarf swept back using a tapered catmull curve in red.

Now I'm adding a tilted blue-tinted windscreen box, and planning a playful roundel or emblem decal on the fuselage sides using small SVG-textured planes.

I'm planning decal details like a roundel, star, and "No.7" text on the fuselage, plus a ring of cylinder head bumps around the cowling front to suggest a radial engine.

I'm deciding against extra pennants and bunting for simplicity, and settling on a whimsical color palette—teal fuselage, cream/yellow wings, copper cowling—then moving to write the fuselage loft code from tail to nose stations.

Calculating positions for struts, wings, and cabane braces to keep everything proportioned and intersecting naturally with the fuselage.

Still working out the pilot figure: positioning the tail wheel, then building the head, goggles, flying cap, and a scarf using curved sweep points for the cockpit occupant.
